other_fabrications.sentence: S2 had a workplace pension with a 5% contribution.

other_fabrications.sentence: S2's team leader contract was signed on a tablet in 2018, and she only has the original paper copy.
other_fabrications.why: She signed something on a tablet when she became team leader (2021). The 2018 document is her original paper contract (L0029).

other_fabrications.sentence: S2's team leader role was confirmed by a certificate from 2023.
other_fabrications.why: The certificate is a 'team leader of the quarter' award (L0052), not confirmation of the role. The line is repeated four times.

other_fabrications.sentence: S2's team leader role ended in 2023, and Gary Whitlock became the operations manager.
other_fabrications.why: Her team leader role did not end in 2023; she held it until her dismissal on 14 August 2026. Gary started in January 2026 (L0057).

other_fabrications.sentence: S2 has mentioned that she has a copy of the February break policy email.
other_fabrications.why: She does not have it; it was on her work email and she was cut off (L0066, L0193).

other_fabrications.sentence: S2 has mentioned that she has a copy of the first aid log.
other_fabrications.why: Marcus filled in the first aid log (L0108). She does not have it, and it is on the DSAR list (L0195).

other_fabrications.sentence: S2's primary objective is to obtain an agreed reference and compensation from Northgate Logistics Limited.
other_fabrications.why: Her main goals are an acknowledgement that they got it wrong and a proper reference; money is 'not the main thing' (L0234-L0235).

other_fabrications.sentence: S1 advised S2 that she has a right to appeal within five working days of the dismissal letter.
other_fabrications.why: The dismissal letter said this (L0158). Daniel gave no such advice; the appeal was already over.

other_fabrications.sentence: S1 advised S2 to send a subject access request to Northgate Logistics Limited.
other_fabrications.why: The firm sends the DSAR; Sophie drafts it (L0195, L0297).

other_fabrications.sentence: S1 is asked to send a timeline of everything S2 has told her today by next Friday, October 8th.
other_fabrications.why: Aisha writes the timeline, by Friday 2 October (L0293). 8 October is the next meeting (L0309).

notes: Next-step dates are mostly right, but the factual content is thin and often wrong: she supposedly holds the Feb email and the first aid log, her role supposedly ended in 2023, a certain 5% pension, and compensation listed among her primary goals. Nothing on the events, the dismissal or the advice.
